headlines.title: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Stock Trades At A Discount Following Its 97% Run
headlines.summary: Johnson & Johnson has delivered strong share gains in recent years, so the key issue now is whether the current valuation is properly backed by the cash the business is expected to generate. Recent trial updates in oncology and medtech add more moving parts to that cash flow picture, which puts extra focus on what the underlying numbers can support. Over the past 3 years, Johnson & Johnson has returned 97.

headlines.title: Medtronic Has Raised Its Dividend for 49 Years. These 2 Rivals Have Even Longer Streaks
headlines.summary: Medtronic's 49-year dividend streak sounds impressive until you meet the two medical device rivals that have been raising payouts even longer, and the differences in yield, valuation, and balance sheet strength could reshape how you think about income investing in this sector.

headlines.title: 4 Arthritis Drug Stocks Investors Should Monitor for Growth Potential
headlines.summary: LLY, NVS, JNJ and ABBV offer arthritis drug growth potential through rising sales, regulatory approvals and clinical advances across inflammatory joint diseases.

headlines.title: CDs or Dividend Stocks: Which Pays Retirees Better Right Now?
headlines.summary: Johnson & Johnson, Procter & Gamble, and Coca-Cola all beat the national CD average on yield, but the real comparison has nothing to do with today's rate and everything to do with what happens to your income over the next decade.

description: Johnson & Johnson, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the research and development, manufacture, and sale of a range of products in the healthcare field worldwide. It operates in two segments, Innovative Medicine and MedTech. The Innovative Medicine segment offers products for various therapeutic areas, such as oncology, immunology, neuroscience, pulmonary hypertension, infectious diseases, and cardiovascular and metabolism distributed through retailers, wholesalers, distributors, hospitals, and healthcare professionals for prescription use. The MedTech segment provides a portfolio of products used in the surgery, orthopedic, cardiovascular, and vision fields distributed through wholesalers, hospitals and retailers, and used in the professional fields by physicians, nurses, hospitals, eye care professionals and clinics. This segment also offers products and enabling technologies that support joint reconstruction, trauma, spine, sports related injuries, and others, as well as open, laparoscopic, and robotic surgical procedures; instrumentation, energy devices, stapling systems, wound closure, biosurgery products, and digital and robotic technologies; breast aesthetics and reconstruction; contact lenses under the ACUVUE brand; intraocular lenses for cataract surgery, and other products used in cataract and refractive procedures under the TECNIS brand. The company was founded in 1886 and is based in New Brunswick, New Jersey.
